overview:
This check monitors [TLS][1] protocol versions, certificate expiration and validity, etc.

**Notes**:

1. Only TCP is supported.
2. Only leaf / end user certificates are verified (not intermediate and root certificates).

**Minimum Agent version:** 6.12.0

[1]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_Layer_Security
setup:
### Installation

The TLS check is included in the [Datadog Agent][2] package.
No additional installation is needed on your server.

### Configuration

<!-- xxx tabs xxx -->
<!-- xxx tab "Host" xxx -->

#### Host

To configure this check for an Agent running on a host:

1. Edit the `tls.d/conf.yaml` file, in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your Agent's configuration directory to start collecting your TLS data. See the [sample tls.d/conf.yaml][3] for all available configuration options.

2. [Restart the Agent][4].

<!-- xxz tab xxx -->
<!-- xxx tab "Containerized" xxx -->

#### Containerized

For containerized environments, see the [Autodiscovery Integration Templates][5] for guidance on applying the parameters below.

| Parameter            | Value                                  |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `<INTEGRATION_NAME>` | `tls`                                  |
| `<INIT_CONFIG>`      | blank or `{}`                          |
| `<INSTANCE_CONFIG>`  | `{"server": "%%host%%", "port":"443"}` |

**Note**: If you are using internal certificates that are not from a well-known, trusted CA, certain metrics may not report to Datadog. Use `tls_verify: false` in your integration template to report all metrics in this instance.

<!-- xxz tab xxx -->
<!-- xxz tabs xxx -->

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][6] and look for `tls` under the Checks section.

metrics.name: tls.issued_days
metrics.description: Day duration of timespan certificate is issued for

metrics.name: tls.issued_seconds
metrics.description: Second duration of timespan certificate is issued for

serviceChecks.name: Can Connect
serviceChecks.description: Returns `CRITICAL` if the Agent is unable to connect to the monitored endpoint, otherwise returns `OK`.

serviceChecks.name: Allowed TLS/SSL version
serviceChecks.description: Returns `CRITICAL` if a connection is made with a protocol version that is not allowed, otherwise returns `OK`.

serviceChecks.name: Certificate validation
serviceChecks.description: Returns `CRITICAL` if the certificate is malformed or does not match the server hostname, otherwise returns `OK`.

serviceChecks.name: Certificate expiration
serviceChecks.description: Returns `CRITICAL` if the certificate has expired or expires in less than `days_critical`/`seconds_critical`, returns `WARNING` if the certificate expires in less than `days_warning`/`seconds_warning`, otherwise returns `OK`.

releaseNotes.notes:
***Changed***:

* Expire downloaded intermediate CA trust after `intermediate_cert_refresh_interval` (60 minutes by default). With `fetch_intermediate_certs` enabled, validation reports CRITICAL when the endpoint requires an expired cached intermediate and its AIA endpoint cannot serve a valid replacement, until trust can be renewed. ([#25363](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25363))

***Fixed***:

* Reload rotated TLS client certificates without restarting the Agent when their contents change. Missing, unreadable, malformed, or mismatched client credentials report CRITICAL validation without certificate-age metrics until a complete valid pair is available, including during non-atomic rotation. Retry TLS context creation if a configured CA bundle is temporarily missing during a rebuild. ([#25363](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25363))

***Security***:

* Fetch AIA intermediate certificates with a fresh credential-free HTTP session, trying TLS first and then plain HTTP fallback. ([#24154](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/24154))

***Added***:

* Update dependencies ([#25284](https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/pull/25284))

***Security***:

***Fixed***:
